channel.title: PostKina — Stories worth sharing
channel.description: Source-led reporting and original context for Europe and the wider world.

item.title: Daily Europe Briefing: Spanish Elections, Turkish Media Crackdown, Ibiza Oil Spill Threat, Brazil-France Trade Spat, and Italian Police Chief Allegations
item.description: Spain's election race concludes with PM Sánchez aiming to defy polls, while Turkey faces scrutiny over a pro-opposition TV channel's alleged destruction. Off Ibiza, a capsized tanker sparks oil spill fears. Brazil pushes back on Macron's "doped" meat claims, and Italy's former police chief posthumously rejects mafia allegations.

item.title: Ukraine Faces Second War Winter Amidst Stalemate and Enduring Resilience
item.description: As Ukraine enters its second full-scale war winter, the nation demonstrates remarkable resilience despite freezing conditions and persistent infrastructure attacks. Front lines remain largely static, raising questions about the conflict's resolution and the sustainability of international support.

item.title: Zelensky Expresses Frustration Over Trump-Putin Relationship and US Stance on Peace Talks
item.description: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky has voiced strong criticism regarding the perceived friendship between Donald Trump and Vladimir Putin, alongside frustration over what he describes as insufficient US pressure on Russia in ongoing peace negotiations.

item.title: Daily Europe Briefing: Depardieu Trial, Ibiza Spill, Migration Networks, Spanish Elections, UK-EU Treaty
item.description: A Paris court rules Gérard Depardieu will stand trial for rape, a diesel tanker capsizes near Ibiza raising environmental fears, and a German man is confronted over alleged migrant boat supply. Spain prepares for snap elections, while a new UK-EU treaty reveals a 10-year termination clause.

item.title: French Mainstream Parties Face Electoral Peril as Extremes Gain Ground Ahead of 2027 Vote
item.description: As France approaches its 2027 presidential election, mainstream political parties are reportedly struggling to coalesce around a clear candidate, risking a significant electoral setback. Current polls indicate a strong lead for figures from the hard-right and hard-left, signaling a potential shift in the nation's political landscape.

item.title: German Boat Dealer Suspected in Major Channel Smuggling Operation
item.description: A BBC investigation has uncovered allegations that a German boat dealer's firm supplied nearly a third of vessels or engines used in English Channel crossings by irregular migrants in early 2026. UK and German authorities are reportedly investigating the cross-border supply chain.

item.title: Daily Europe Briefing: Ukraine War Spreads, Pelicot Controversy, and Europe's Shifting Mobility
item.description: Ukraine's conflict extends to Libya, a French publisher faces backlash over promotional tactics, and tiny cars gain traction across Europe. This briefing also examines the UK's ongoing EU debate and other key developments shaping the continent.

item.title: Ukraine Claims Five Russian Jets Hit in Airfield Strike
item.description: Ukraine's military intelligence claims a strike on Russia's Savasleyka airfield damaged five military jets. The base reportedly hosts aircraft used for launching hypersonic missiles and glide bombs, marking a significant potential blow to Russian air capabilities.

item.title: Zimbabwean Convicted in South Africa for Attempting to Join Ukraine Conflict
item.description: A Zimbabwean citizen has been convicted in South Africa for attempting to participate in the conflict in Ukraine, highlighting the global reach of the war and the complex issue of foreign fighters. Ukraine claims hundreds of Africans have been recruited to fight for Russia.

item.title: Daily Europe Briefing: Russia's War Toll, Spanish Election, Sarkozy Trial, and Papal Revelations
item.description: Russia's war in Ukraine reveals a staggering human cost, while Spain faces a pivotal election. Former French President Sarkozy and his wife head to trial, and late Pope Francis' diary entries spark spiritual debate.

item.title: Russian Murmansk Governor Detained in Rare Criminal Case
item.description: Andrei Chibis, the governor of Russia's northern Murmansk region, has been detained in a criminal case, marking the first such incident involving a regional leader in five years. The development signals a rare legal action against a high-ranking official.

item.title: NATO Chief Warns of Space Threats Amid Reports of Russian Nuclear Satellite
item.description: NATO Secretary General Jens Stoltenberg addresses concerns over potential Russian deployment of a nuclear weapon in space, vowing a robust defense strategy.

item.title: Daily Europe Briefing: Daily Europe Briefing - November 24, 2026
item.description: The EU's Migration Pact falls short, relocating only 1,283 asylum seekers in its first year against a 30,000 target. Visegrád Four leaders challenge the EU budget, while France grapples with ongoing protests. A major fire also hit Zanzibar hotels.

item.title: Belgium's Skies Grounded Amid Widespread Cost-of-Living Strike
item.description: Belgium experienced significant air travel disruption as a nationwide cost-of-living strike led to flight cancellations. This industrial action is the latest in a series of protests amid ongoing government struggles to finalize a national budget.

item.title: France's Ultra-Left: A Radical Challenge to the Republic
item.description: France is grappling with a resurgent ultra-left movement, whose activists declare their aim is to dismantle capitalism, not the nation itself. President Emmanuel Macron's government views these groups as a profound threat, accusing them of sedition and attempting to destabilize the Republic amidst escalating street protests and ideological clashes.

item.title: Daily Europe Briefing: Libya Ship Attack, Ukraine Strikes, COP31 Stalemate, and North Korea's Stance
item.description: A Russian naval vessel capsizes in Libya after a suspected drone attack, while Ukraine grapples with the aftermath of Russian strikes. Meanwhile, COP31 climate talks conclude without a deal, and North Korea's leader emphasizes sovereignty after declining talks with former US President Trump.

item.title: EU Affirms Commitment to 'Closest Possible Relationship' with UK for Prosperity
item.description: The European Union has reiterated its ambition for the "closest possible relationship" with the United Kingdom, emphasizing a shared goal of "greater prosperity" as both entities navigate their post-Brexit future.

item.title: Digital Camouflage: Yandex Maps Accused of Obscuring Russian Military Sites with 'Fake Forests'
item.description: Russia's dominant mapping service, Yandex Maps, is under scrutiny following reports by the BBC detailing the appearance of artificial forest imagery over locations suspected of housing military installations, suggesting a deliberate effort to conceal sensitive sites.

item.title: Daily Europe Briefing: Gulf of Finland Attack, Danish Accusations, and UK-Ukraine Solidarity
item.description: A drone attack in the Gulf of Finland, Denmark's accusation of a Russian assassination plot, UK's strong support for Ukraine, new UK-EU agreements, and a high-profile summit's limited substance dominate Europe's agenda.

item.title: Zelensky Defends Crimean Bridge Strikes as 'Fair Response' to Russian Attacks
item.description: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky has characterized recent strikes on the Crimean Bridge as a "fair response" to Russia's extensive aerial campaign targeting Ukrainian bridges. His comments came during a meeting with UK politician Wes Streeting, highlighting Kyiv's retaliatory stance.

item.title: Europe Prepares Unified Stance for Talks with Russia on Ukraine Conflict
item.description: European leaders signal a united front for negotiations with Russia, aiming to end the war in Ukraine. The Berlin summit marks a pivotal moment as allies outline a coordinated strategy and set expectations for future talks.

item.title: Daily Europe Briefing: Police Brutality, Ukraine Strikes, Depardieu Probe, Protests, and Brexit Deal
item.description: Europe grapples with a range of critical developments: a landmark ruling on police racism in France, renewed Russian missile attacks on Kyiv, sexual assault allegations against Gérard Depardieu, widespread cost-of-living protests, and an anticipated new Brexit agreement for Northern Ireland.

item.title: Russian Missile Strikes Poland Amid Allied Military Drills, Warsaw Calls It 'Provocation'
item.description: A Russian missile impacted Polish territory, prompting Prime Minister Donald Tusk to label the incident a "provocation" from Moscow. The strike, which caused no injuries or damage, occurred while Ukraine's allies conducted military exercises.

item.title: Kyiv Bridges Damaged in Russian Missile Barrage
item.description: Multiple bridges in Kyiv sustained damage during a significant Russian missile attack, resulting in casualties and disruption. The strikes followed Ukraine's recent operation targeting the Crimean Bridge.

item.title: Daily Europe Briefing: Geopolitical Security, UK-EU Relations, and Human Resilience
item.description: A Russian national faces espionage charges in the US, suspected of targeting a defence company crucial to Ukraine's support. Meanwhile, a prominent UK politician considers closer EU alignment. Also, a charity car rally concludes, a football legend retires, and a tennis player shares a powerful mental health story.

item.title: Van Gogh Masterpiece Fetches Record $190.4M After Nazi-Era Provenance Dispute
item.description: Vincent van Gogh's 'Châtaigniers en fleurs,' painted in 1890, has fetched a record $190.4 million at Christie's, following an undisclosed settlement over its complex Nazi-era provenance involving the Rothschild family and heirs of a German Jewish banker.

item.title: Crimean Bridge Traffic Halted After Reported Attack
item.description: Traffic on the Crimean Bridge was suspended following a reported attack, according to Russian authorities. This marks another incident targeting the vital link between Russia and occupied Crimea, raising regional tensions.

item.title: Daily Europe Briefing: Ukraine's Underground Front, Cold Case Justice, and High-Profile Allegations
item.description: Ukrainian forces engage Russian troops in subterranean tunnels in Kharkiv, adapting to drone warfare. Meanwhile, France sees justice in a decades-old child abuse case, and Spanish courts investigate allegations against Julio Iglesias. New footage also sheds light on the Crimea Bridge collapse.

item.title: Trump, Putin, and Xi Hold Historic Handshake Ahead of China Summit
item.description: U.S., Russian, and Chinese leaders exchanged a symbolic handshake in Beijing, marking the first joint meeting of their heads of state. The gesture precedes a high‑stakes summit that could reshape global power dynamics.

item.title: Historic Summit Leaves Putin on a High Stage but Offers No Strategic Gain
item.description: A rare gathering of the US, China and Russia leaders on 18 November 2026 gave Vladimir Putin a prominent platform, yet analysts say it does not translate into a decisive advantage for Moscow in the Ukraine war.

item.title: Daily Europe Briefing: Kyiv Strikes, Spanish Election, and Regional Tensions
item.description: Russia targets Kyiv bridges as Spain prepares for a pivotal election. A Russian military plane crashes, and dozens are injured in a Prague train collision. Tensions rise in Asia following alleged Russian airspace incursions, impacting global security.

item.title: Kyiv's Seven-Stage Assault Inflicts Major Damage on Crimean Bridge
item.description: The Kerch Bridge, a critical symbol of Russia's occupation of Ukraine, has sustained significant damage following a sophisticated seven-stage attack attributed to Kyiv, according to recent reports. The incident marks a major escalation in the ongoing conflict.

item.title: Crimean Bridge Damaged in Overnight Incident, Russia Vows Reconstruction
item.description: A section of the Kerch Strait Bridge, connecting Crimea to mainland Russia, has been damaged. Ukraine claims responsibility for the operation, which it states took weeks of planning. Moscow has pledged to repair the vital infrastructure.

item.title: Daily Europe Briefing: Migrant Hub, Depardieu Appeal, Ukraine Strikes, and Airspace Alerts Dominate Briefing
item.description: Five EU nations announce a Rwanda migrant centre, Gérard Depardieu drops his appeal, Russia strikes Kyiv bridges, and Japan scrambles jets amid airspace incursions.

item.title: Crimea Bridge Struck Amid Russia's Claim of Record Drone Onslaught
item.description: A critical bridge connecting mainland Russia to Crimea has reportedly been hit, coinciding with Russia's assertion of the largest Ukrainian drone attack of the war, involving over 2,000 unmanned aerial vehicles. Kyiv simultaneously experienced a record 17 air raid alerts.

item.title: Gulf Tensions Escalate: US and Iran Near 'All-Out War' Amid Increased Attacks
item.description: A sudden surge in Iranian attacks on shipping in the Strait of Hormuz, coupled with intensifying exchanges of fire and the deployment of a third US aircraft carrier, signals a dangerous escalation in US-Iran tensions, pushing the region closer to widespread conflict.

item.title: Daily Europe Briefing: Europe Briefing: Starlink, Media Freedom, and Oligarch Dreams
item.description: Developments across Europe include Ukrainian calls for Starlink access, Czech protests over public media funding, and Paris police restrictions on demonstrations. Meanwhile, Russian tycoons reportedly envision a post-Putin era, and football legend Ronaldinho makes a comeback.

item.title: Australia and Philippines Forge New Defence Pact Amid South China Sea Tensions
item.description: Australia and the Philippines have formalized a new defence agreement, deepening military cooperation as Manila navigates persistent tensions with China in the South China Sea. The pact is part of a broader strategy by the Philippines to bolster regional alliances.

item.title: Europe Confronts Widespread Cyberattacks, Emergency Summit Underway
item.description: An unprecedented wave of coordinated cyberattacks targeting critical infrastructure across multiple European Union member states has prompted an emergency summit in Brussels. Leaders are convening to address the escalating digital threat and formulate a unified response.

item.title: Daily Europe Briefing: Regulatory Fines, Art Disputes, Corruption Probes, and Sports Sanctions
item.description: Italy levies a massive fine against Meta for privacy breaches, a $180m Van Gogh auction faces legal challenge, Hungarian authorities uncover significant funds in an anti-corruption probe, and Estonia joins the ban on Russian athletes.

item.title: Trump, Putin, Xi to Hold Historic Nuclear Talks in China
item.description: The White House has announced an unprecedented joint meeting between US President Trump, Russian President Putin, and Chinese President Xi Jinping in China next week, with nuclear weapons reduction as a key agenda item. This historic summit marks a rare convergence of global powers.

item.title: Zelensky Claims US Floated Donbas Cession for NATO Membership
item.description: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky has claimed that US envoys proposed Ukraine cede the Donbas region in exchange for NATO membership, as part of efforts to end the ongoing conflict with Russia. The revelation raises significant questions about diplomatic strategies.

item.title: Daily Europe Briefing: Daily Europe Briefing
item.description: Germany expands intelligence powers to counter hybrid threats, an aide to a Ukrainian ex-PM is wounded in Moscow, an inquest opens into a boy's death in Cyprus, Eurovision expands to Asia, and a deadly shooting rocks Krakow.

item.title: Putin Escalates Demands for Ukraine Peace, Citing European Security
item.description: Russian President Vladimir Putin is reportedly escalating his demands for a peace settlement with Ukraine, now incorporating broader European security concerns into negotiations, a development Moscow views as a strategic win.

item.title: Zelensky Welcomes European Inclusion in Russia-Ukraine Peace Talks
item.description: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky has endorsed a US initiative to bring European leaders into future peace negotiations with Russia, citing Ukraine's ambition to join the European Union as a crucial factor for their involvement.

item.title: Daily Europe Briefing: Baltic Drone Attack, Finnish Embassy Viral Moment, Cyprus Charges, Krakow Incident, Office Conversions
item.description: A drone attack on a Russian warship in the Baltic, a Finnish embassy's viral planning day, charges against a British soldier in Cyprus, an incident in Krakow, and the conversion of office buildings into homes feature in today's briefing.

item.title: Italian Schools Evacuated Again After Second Day of Bomb Threats
item.description: For the second consecutive day, schools across Italy have been evacuated following bomb threats, prompting heightened security measures and raising concerns about student safety and the motives behind the alerts.

item.title: U.S. Envoys Arrive in Moscow Ahead of Ukraine Talks with President Putin
item.description: Jared Kushner and Steve Witkoff landed in Moscow on Thursday, preparing for a high‑stakes meeting with Vladimir Putin that could shape the future of the Ukraine conflict. The U.S. delegation will soon head to Dublin to join President Volodymyr Zelensky in a separate summit.

item.title: Daily Europe Briefing: Europe Briefing: Ukraine Power Crisis, Barcelona Strikes, School Threats, and Tennis Shocks
item.description: A look at the day's top European stories, including Ukraine's critical power situation, protests in Spain, bomb threats in schools across Italy, Scotland, and Northern Ireland, and a significant upset at the WTA Finals.

item.title: Russia-Ukraine Talks on Post-War Security Conclude Without Breakthrough in Abu Dhabi
item.description: High-level discussions between Russian and Ukrainian representatives in Abu Dhabi, centered on establishing a post-war security framework for Europe, have concluded without achieving a significant breakthrough. The talks precede separate meetings.
